findings.title: Caution falsely says the Operator fails without rolling-updates
findings.body: The new caution says that during preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or the Keycloak Operator will fail. That contradicts both the note later in this same section and the operator test added in this PR. UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the update strategy is null and does not set spec.features.enabled to rolling-updates. Those cases still call deployKeycloak with wait-for-ready, and a cache max-count change is expected to roll rather than fail. So a normal Keycloak CR reconciles, becomes ready, and applies the documented 26.1-compatible default (recreate only on image change, roll on other config) with the preview feature off. The feature is only enabled in that test when spec.update.strategy is set explicitly. As written, the caution tells every Operator user that an upgrade breaks unless they turn on a preview feature, which will cause unnecessary preview opt-in or blocked upgrades. Narrow the warning to explicit spec.update usage, or change the test if fail-closed is actually required.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented as an upgrade decision
findings.body: The new exit-code row says code 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because `rolling-updates` is disabled. That is the same decision wording as exit code 3, and the paragraph above the table says these codes are how automation determines the upgrade type. The implementation does not decide compatibility: both update-compatibility check and update-compatibility metadata print "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and exit 4 before reading metadata or comparing versions. The only other upgrade type this guide defines is recreate (shut the deployment down before applying config). A pipeline that treats "rolling is not possible" as that outcome will take an unnecessary outage when the flag was merely omitted. Describe code 4 as a precondition failure, state that the upgrade type was not determined, and note that the metadata subcommand returns 4 as well; the table currently sits only under the check command.

findings.title: Changed exit codes 3 and 4 are never asserted
findings.body: This PR changes CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and adds FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, and the guide tells users to branch automation on those codes. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the disabled-feature sentence and never asserts the process exit code is 4; it also covers only the metadata subcommand, not check. testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility log line and never asserts exit code 3. CLIResult.assertError succeeds for any non-zero status, so leaving recreate at 4, or picocli.exit collapsing the custom code to 1, would still pass. That docs-vs-code mismatch (docs already said 3, the constant was 4) is exactly what this PR is fixing, and nothing locks the new contract.
